selector_prompt.system:
You are the internal material-dataset selector inside a scientific TMM
harness. This is not route planning and you must not redesign the route.
Return exactly one JSON object and no markdown:
{"selections":[{"request_id":"material_01","selected_rank":1,"provider":"rii_sqlite","dataset_id":562,"reason":"..."}]}

The user question is authoritative. Each request contains candidates already
retrieved from the local MaterialRegistry and sorted by three equal physical
metrics: target-band coverage, n/k completeness, and sampling density. Rank 1
is the most physically reliable candidate; lower rank means less reliable.
Choose exactly one candidate from the supplied list for every request. Never
invent, rename, or edit a provider or dataset_id. The selected_rank must point
to the selected array element, and provider/dataset_id must copy that element.

Material identity, stoichiometry, explicit material state/preparation, and an
explicit requested source are hard constraints. A candidate with
formula_exact=false or semantic_match=same_element_family is not an allowed
substitute for a formula request. SiO is not SiO2, even if the SiO2 candidate
has better physical coverage. When several candidates satisfy the hard
constraints, select the highest-ranked one (usually rank 1). If no candidate
satisfies them, return selected_rank:null, provider:null, dataset_id:null and
reason:"needs_confirmation" for that request.

plan.planning_summary: This control axis tests whether thickness optimization alone on a fixed quarter-wave-derived periodic stack can achieve the dual-band dichroic performance (high visible reflectance, high IR transmittance) using only HfO2/SiO2. The design draws from recalled thin-film optics principles: quarter-wave stacks produce high-reflectance bands centered at the design wavelength with transmission windows at harmonic multiples. I would have wanted to look up exact n/k dispersion data for HfO2 and SiO2 across 400-1565 nm, typical absorption losses in HfO2 below 500 nm, and published dichroic filter designs for similar band separations to validate the starting topology.

routes.title: Thickness-Optimized Quarter-Wave Dichroic Stack for Visible Rejection and IR Transmission
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A 24-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 stack with individual layer thicknesses optimized from quarter-wave starting values at 550 nm can simultaneously achieve high reflectance in 400-700 nm and high transmittance in 1530-1565 nm without requiring chirped or aperiodic layer sequences.
routes.design_principle: Quarter-wave dielectric stacks produce a high-reflectance photonic bandgap centered at the design wavelength. The first transmission window appears at approximately 3× the center wavelength for a standard quarter-wave stack. By centering the reflective band at 550 nm (middle of 400-700 nm), the transmission window should naturally fall near 1500-1700 nm, covering the 1530-1565 nm signal band. Thickness optimization refines the band edges and reduces ripple.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | Fused Silica Substrate (24 layers total, alternating high-low index starting with HfO2)
design_variables: Individual thickness of each of the 24 layers (t1 through t24, in nm)
Starting point: quarter-wave optical thickness at 550 nm center wavelength
soft_objectives: Maximize average reflectance in 400-700 nm band
Maximize average transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band
Minimize transmittance ripple in 1530-1565 nm band
Keep total layer count at exactly 24 (within 30-layer constraint)
manufacturing_considerations: Total layer count fixed at 24, leaving 6 layers of margin within the 30-layer maximum
Quarter-wave starting thicknesses approximately 65-70 nm for HfO2 and 90-95 nm for SiO2 at 550 nm center
All layers are standard evaporated/sputtered dielectric thicknesses achievable with conventional coating equipment
No sub-quarter-wave or super-quarter-wave extreme thicknesses expected to be required
theory_basis: Recalled: Quarter-wave stack reflectance bandwidth scales with index contrast ratio (nH/nL); HfO2/SiO2 provides approximately 2.0/1.45 ≈ 1.38 contrast
Recalled: First transmission window for quarter-wave stack appears at approximately 3× the center wavelength (λ0/4 stack transmits near 3λ0/4 optical path)
Recalled: Peak reflectance increases with number of layer pairs; 12 pairs should provide >95% reflectance in the stopband for this index contrast
Recalled: Individual layer thickness tuning can shift band edges and reduce passband ripple without changing material pair
Recalled: Starting from quarter-wave design provides a physically meaningful baseline that optimization can refine
expected_advantages: Simple periodic topology is easier to manufacture than chirped or aperiodic designs
Quarter-wave starting point provides good initial performance, reducing optimization iterations needed
24 layers leaves manufacturing margin within the 30-layer constraint
HfO2 and SiO2 are standard, well-characterized coating materials with low absorption in both bands
known_risks: Uncertain: Exact refractive index values for hfo2 and sio2 across 400-1565 nm - would need to verify from material_catalog datasets
Uncertain: Whether HfO2 has significant absorption below 450 nm that would reduce visible reflectance - would need to check extinction coefficient data
Uncertain: Whether 12 pairs provides sufficient visible reflectance (>90%) or if more pairs would be needed - may require increasing to 14-15 pairs
Uncertain: Incidence angle not specified in request; assuming normal incidence (0°) but satellite applications may have off-axis rays - angular sensitivity not tested in this route
Uncertain: Polarization state not specified; assuming unpolarized or testing both TE/TM - polarization splitting at oblique angles not addressed

Trade-off given up: Not exploring chirped or aperiodic layer sequences that might provide sharper band edges; not exploring alternative center wavelengths; not exploring different starting layer (SiO2-first vs HfO2-first)
routes.execution_request_english: Design a 24-layer periodic dielectric stack for dichroic filtering. Stack structure: Air incident side, then alternating HfO2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) layers starting with HfO2, ending with SiO2 (Lemarchand) before fused silica substrate. Total 24 layers (12 HfO2 + 12 SiO2 (Lemarchand)). Optimize individual thickness of each layer. Starting point: quarter-wave optical thickness at 550 nm center wavelength (HfO2 ~69 nm, SiO2 (Lemarchand) ~95 nm based on recalled indices n_HfO2≈2.0, n_SiO2 (Lemarchand)≈1.45). Wavelength bands: maximize reflectance in 400-700 nm, maximize transmittance in 1530-1565 nm. Incidence angle: 0 degrees (normal). Polarization: unpolarized (average of TE and TM). Manufacturing constraint: exactly 24 layers, within 30-layer maximum. Materials: hfo2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) from catalog. Substrate: fused silica (SiO2 (Lemarchand)).

unresolved_decisions: Exact refractive index dispersion for hfo2 and sio2 across full 400-1565 nm range must be read from material_catalog datasets at execution time
Whether HfO2 extinction coefficient is negligible in 400-500 nm range - absorption would reduce visible reflectance performance
Optimal starting layer (HfO2-first vs SiO2-first) not tested; chose HfO2-first based on recalled convention for high-index-first stacks on low-index substrates

plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: If this control route fails to achieve best_target_score > 0.7 after full optimization, the fundamental quarter-wave periodic topology may be insufficient for this band separation ratio (700/400 nm visible vs 1565/1530 nm IR), and a literature-grounded route exploring chirped stacks or alternative topologies would be needed.

expected_observations: best_target_score should increase across optimization rounds as layer thicknesses converge toward optimal values
tightest_margin should remain non-negative across rounds, indicating physically valid candidates throughout
valid_candidates count should remain high (not dropping to zero), indicating the search space is well-bounded
If hypothesis is correct: final design shows reflectance >85% in 400-700 nm band AND transmittance >90% in 1530-1565 nm band
If hypothesis is incorrect: best_target_score plateaus at low value indicating fundamental topology limitation, or one band performance degrades to improve the other
stop_conditions: If best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the thickness optimization axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best thickness set
If valid_candidates drops below 5 for two consecutive rounds, relax thickness bounds by 20% and continue; if still failing after relaxation, stop and flag topology may need revision
If tightest_margin falls below -0.1 for any candidate, that candidate is invalid but continue searching; if all candidates invalid for two rounds, stop and report infeasible starting bounds
